title: COIL-20
blurb: 5 objects from the COIL-20 photo set, each shot every 10° as it spins on a turntable. One view is raw pixels; the other is DINOv2, a vision model. A spinning object ought to trace a circle.

notes.neighbors: The teacup changes friends most: from most angles it is a plain bowl, and the handle comes and goes.
notes.rips: Watch the edges, not the blobs: each object’s ring of photos closes on its own somewhere around ε ≈ 0.3–0.4 and fills in again near 0.5.

about.name: Columbia Object Image Library (COIL-20)
about.quote: The second, [processed], contains images for all of the objects in which the background has been discarded (and the images consist of the smallest square that contains the object).
about.label: Columbia CAVE

about.name: DINOv2
about.quote: DINOv2 models produce high-performance visual features that can be directly employed with classifiers as simple as linear layers on a variety of computer vision tasks
about.label: Meta FAIR

here: Here: 5 objects × 36 angles (every 10°) from the processed set, as 32×32 pixels (A) and DINOv2 embeddings (B).
